title.narrative: Envelop-2: Life-saving humanitarian assistance to address the most critical needs of internally displaced people, returning to Eastern Tigray.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe post-COHA humanitarian context in Tigray remains critical. Fear of relapse to war and attendant challenges in providing unfettered humanitarian assistance to the returning IDPs has worsened the dynamism in the region. The context holds true across the four critically affected woredas in Eastern Tigray. Weak health infrastructure, destruction of the water facilities, exposure to protection concerns, widespread malnutrition situation in the woredas still persists. According to the multisectoral assessment report compiled by OCHA in July 2025, most health facilities in those woredas are non-functional and/or partially functional. The collapse of the health services has exacerbated the nutrition situation pervaded by acute malnutrition cases. Severely damaged Wash infrastructure has exposed nearly 85 percent of the population in those woredas to a critically low access to water. 76 percent of the communities are reported to have limited access to latrines while 38 percent are none, worsening disease outbreak risks. Almost all the data from the report indicated that 100 percent of the respondents in the IDPs and host communities feel unsafe, with heightened risk of GBV, violence and concerns at 21 percent of the total respondents in the woredas. Overall, massive humanitarian crisis with limited humanitarian presence in the woredas with Zalambasa’s case being the catastrophic one while Erob, Gulomekeda and Adigrat standing at the extreme level of crisis is identified by the report. These multipronged challenges with wider gaps in all types’ humanitarian services provide the basis for integrated multisectoral intervention.ltbrgtThe scope of intervention of the project involves addressing the multipronged challenges through multisectoral interventions to the general protection, health, nutrition and wash needs of the affected population by responding to the critical humanitarian gaps in the woredas. It will basically focus on addressing ltbrgt General protection focusing on, protection monitoring, Cash interventions to minimize exposure to protection risks and negative coping mechanisms as well as vulnerability screening engagementsltbrgt Nutrition focused on establishing and deploying mobile health and nutrition team (MHNT), conduct mass screening for acute malnutrition cases, capacity building by training HWs on IMAM ltbrgt Health focused on provision of capacity building trainings to the HWs and Village health Leaders (VHL), conduct health education sessions, support prevention of outbreak of diseases ltbrgt WASH focused rehabilitation of waterpoints, repair and maintenance of water schemes, conduct assessment of sanitation facilities in schools and health care facilitiesltbrgtThese activities will be implemented using time-bound implementation strategy that will be conducted over 9 months in three important component phases. Phase one entails a one-month implementation of activities focused on inception and rapid assessment. Phase 2 involves 2-7 months activities focused on rolling out the full spectrum of the activities towards intensive service delivery. Phase 3 is basically implementation of activities that focused in evaluation, transition, linkage and reporting of the project. ltbrgtlt/pgt
